skills.name: Upjohn
skills.description: Properly identifies representation and role with the Company, and that they cannot give the employee legal advice. This must always be part of the very beginning of the interview.
skills.reason: At T2 the interviewer says 'I represent the company, not you,' but never states that counsel cannot give the witness legal advice or that counsel is not the witness's own lawyer, and does not explain the purpose of the investigation.

skills.name: Privilege
skills.description: Properly explains that the Company controls the privilege and determines how it is shared.
skills.reason: At T2 the interviewer explains that the privilege belongs to the company and that the company may decide to share what the witness says. It does not add that the witness should not share the substance of the interview.

skills.name: Relationship
skills.description: Establishes rapport and interview expectations. This includes: establishes an appropriate professional tone; explains how the interview will proceed; encourages complete answers; instructs the witness that they can speculate, they just need to say when they do; invites the witness to distinguish between recollection and uncertainty.
skills.reason: Rapport and expectations are minimal. The interviewer does not explain how the interview will proceed, does not say speculation is allowed if flagged, and does not invite the witness to separate recollection from uncertainty.

skills.name: Confirmation
skills.description: Checks the witness understood the Upjohn warning and answers their questions, if any.
skills.reason: At T2 the interviewer asks 'Any questions?' and the witness replies 'No. Go ahead.' There is no check that the witness understood the warning.

skills.name: Closing
skills.description: Closes by confirming there is "nothing else", next steps, a confidentiality reminder, and a reminder to keep records.
skills.reason: At T80 the interviewer asks whether there is anything else the Committee should know, and at T86 reminds the witness to keep documents and keep the matter confidential. Next steps and a no-contact instruction for other witnesses are missing.

moments.text: I represent the company, not you. What we discuss is privileged, but the privilege belongs to the company, and the company may decide to share what you tell me. Any questions?
No. Go ahead.
Is there anything I haven't asked about that you think the Committee should know?
Please keep any related documents and keep this confidential. Thanks.

skills.name: Narrative Development
skills.description: Lets the witness walk through what happened.
skills.reason: Open prompts such as 'How did LJM1 come about in 1999?' (T10) and 'Tell me about the June 28, 1999 Board meeting. What did you present?' (T16) let the witness give extended accounts (T11, T17).

skills.name: Funneling
skills.description: Moves in a sensible order from general to specific questions.
skills.reason: The interview moves from role (T4) to people (T6-T9) to LJM1 (T10), then to Board approvals, Chewco, LJM2 controls, Raptors, personal interests and the Chewco buyout. The order is sensible, though it jumps topics at times.

skills.name: Clarity
skills.description: Asks clear questions and avoids compound, ambiguous, or legalistic questions.
skills.reason: Several questions are compound or tag questions, such as 'Who negotiated it on both sides, and did anyone object?' (T22), 'Chewco was formed in 1997 to buy CalPERS' interest in JEDI, wasn't it?' (T24), and 'You negotiated the Chewco buyout yourself, didn't you?' (T68).

skills.name: Professionalism
skills.description: Stays neutral, polite and in control.
skills.reason: The interviewer stays polite and in control throughout. Some challenges are pointed, such as 'Isn't that inconsistent with what you told the Board?' (T58), but the tone never becomes hostile.

skills.name: Adaptability
skills.description: Changes technique based on the witness's answers rather than staying only with the outline.
skills.reason: The interviewer adapts to the witness's answers: they follow up on 'I believe he told the Board' with 'How do you know?' (T34), pursue 'I assumed it was followed' (T38-T39), narrow the foundation questions after 'I'd have to check its records' (T55-T56), and confront the Southampton contribution once the witness denies personal interest (T52-T58).

moments.text: How did LJM1 come about in 1999?
Tell me about the June 28, 1999 Board meeting. What did you present?
Who negotiated it on both sides, and did anyone object?
Chewco was formed in 1997 to buy CalPERS' interest in JEDI, wasn't it?
You negotiated the Chewco buyout yourself, didn't you?
So you were involved, weren't you?

areas.name: Fact Development, Source Identification, & Credibility Testing

skills.name: Ensures Credibility
skills.description: Recognizes and follows up on incomplete, evasive, or inconsistent answers.
skills.reason: Evasive answers are repeatedly followed up, including the Kopper selection (T28-T30), the Skilling approval (T32-T35), the Foundation (T52-T61), the Code question (T62-T63) and the tax payment (T74-T79). The interviewer does not follow up on the witness's admission that some approvals were papered after closing (T43).

skills.name: Material Facts
skills.description: Identifies the who, what, when, and how.
skills.reason: The interviewer asks who decided the Foundation investment (T60), who else invested (T64), who approved the tax payment (T76) and when the approvals were signed (T42). Raptor return figures remain unresolved.

skills.name: Memory Refreshing
skills.description: Tries other ways when the witness can't remember.
skills.reason: When the witness says 'I don't have the exact figures' (T47) and 'I'd have to look at the sheet' (T43), the interviewer asks for approximations but does not show the approval sheet or any other record to refresh recall.

skills.name: Establishes Knowledge
skills.description: Separates what the witness personally knows from speculation, secondhand information, or inferences.
skills.reason: The interviewer separates personal knowledge from hearsay with 'How do you know Mr. Skilling told the Board?' (T34) and 'How do you know they reviewed every transaction?' (T38), and the witness concedes 'I don't know that personally' (T35).

skills.name: Other Sources
skills.description: Identifies additional witnesses.
skills.reason: At T82 the interviewer asks who else to speak with, and the witness names Causey, Buy, Glisan, Kopper, Andersen and Vinson & Elkins.

skills.name: Other Evidence
skills.description: Identifies other documents such as communications, reports, notes, or other relevant records.
skills.reason: At T84 the interviewer asks what documents to review, and the witness names approval sheets and committee materials. The interviewer does not ask about investor reports, communications or the tax payment file, even though the witness says 'I'd want to see the investor reports' (T51).

skills.name: Tests Certainty
skills.description: Examines how certain the witness is about their memory or a fact.
skills.reason: The interviewer does not probe how certain the witness is. Vague answers such as 'It may have. It was a small amount' (T57) and 'I may have had a call with them about it' (T79) are not tested for certainty.

skills.name: Follow-Up
skills.description: Recognizes material responses and follows up on them.
skills.reason: Material responses are followed up, including the Southampton distribution (T58), the $10.5 million note (T72), the foundation's investment decision (T60-T61) and the tax payment (T74-T79). The 'papered after closing' admission at T43 is not followed up.

moments.text: How do you know Mr. Skilling told the Board?
How do you know they reviewed every transaction?
When did they sign it, relative to the closing?
Witness says some approvals were papered after a deal closed; the interviewer moves on without asking which deals or who decided this.
What investments connected to LJM1 did the foundation make in early 2000?
Who approved the payment?
Who else should we speak with to understand these transactions?
What documents should we look at?

skills.name: Effective Selection
skills.description: Selects and contextualizes documents effectively, and properly authenticates the document.
skills.reason: The interviewer refers to the Southampton Place agreement (T58) and an 'Andy' note (T72) with some context, but does not ask the witness to authenticate or identify either document before using it.

skills.name: Narrative
skills.description: Gets the witness's story first, before using conflicting evidence.
skills.reason: At T52-T57 the interviewer first gets the witness's account of the foundation's investments before presenting the Southampton agreement at T58. The Chewco buyout challenge at T68 comes before the witness's own account of it.

skills.name: Accuracy
skills.description: Describes the document accurately.
skills.reason: The figures put to the witness are accurate: the $25,000 contribution and $4.5 million distribution (T58), the 193, 278 and 2,500 percent returns (T66) and the $10.5 million note (T72). The interviewer does not state what each document says about the Board representation.

skills.name: Avoid Initial Conclusion
skills.description: Separates the document from inferences or conclusions, unless the witness takes an unreasonable stance.
skills.reason: The interviewer draws conclusions before the document is established, such as 'So you were involved, weren't you?' (T72) and 'Isn't that inconsistent with what you told the Board?' (T58). The T68 accusation is also made before any evidence is presented.

skills.name: Fairness
skills.description: Provides the witness with a fair opportunity to explain any inconsistencies or disagreements with the document.
skills.reason: After challenges, the interviewer lets the witness explain: the Foundation distinction (T59), the decision to invest (T60-T61), and 'Being informed isn't the same as negotiating' (T73).

moments.text: This is the Southampton Place partnership agreement. It shows a $25,000 contribution from your family foundation, and our information is the foundation received about $4.5 million about six weeks later. Isn't that inconsistent with what you told the Board?
Witness responds that the Foundation is not him and that the Board statement concerned his GP economics, so the interviewer gives him a fair chance to explain.
This note to 'Andy' mentions $10.5 million for the buyout. So you were involved, weren't you?

tips: Before we go further, which approval sheets were signed after the deals closed, and who decided to paper them?
Before I ask about this agreement, what do you recognize it to be, when did you first see it, and what was its purpose?
